# fal raises serverless H100 rate to $2.49/hr, adds GB200 GPU, doubles MiniMax video pricing

By Rob Litterst, Co-founder, PricingSaaS

Published Oct 2, 2026

## What changed

fal's serverless GPU pricing moved across the board: H100 instances rose from $1.89 to $2.49 per hour (up 32%), B300 instances rose from $4.49 to $5.99 per hour (up 33%), and a new GB200 GPU tier was added to the lineup. Separately, MiniMax's H3 Max video model saw its per-second generation rate double, from $0.025 to $0.05.

...

For teams building on fal, this is a direct cost-of-goods increase on two of its most-used GPU tiers plus a 2x jump on one of its video models - margin that has to be absorbed or passed through to end customers. For fal, layering in GB200 support signals it's racing to keep pace with Nvidia's newest hardware generation while monetizing the older fleet harder. Watch whether this is the start of a broader repricing across fal's remaining GPU and model catalog, given it's now made three pricing moves in ten weeks, or whether this settles back into the roughly 30-day cadence its track record shows.

...

This is fal's third real pricing change since tracking began in late July — coming just a day after it finished filling out its Audio and 3D model API price lists on Oct 1 — and its second GPU rate hike since the H100 list price moved to $4.50/hr in early August. Price increases are everywhere in the index right now: Shipday's Enterprise tier jumped 40%, Cumul raised its USD plan 25%, and Hedra hiked its Individual plan all landed in the same late-September window. Most of those are SaaS seat pricing; fal's move extends the same pressure to raw GPU-hour and per-second inference rates, the cost layer underneath everyone else's AI pricing.

It lands one day after fal's previous change, "fal publishes Audio and 3D model API pricing, expands video/image tables to 10 endpoints" (Oct 1, 2026). Before that Pulse recorded "fal: H100 GPU list price increase ($3.99→$4.50/h)" (Aug 5, 2026). fal has been tracked since 2026-07-15.

results.title: B300 prices are not crashing. They are splitting in two. — CheapestGPU
highlights:
The spot prints are real. On October 8, Nebius moved preemptible B300 to dynamic spot pricing with a floor of $0.99 per GPU-hour, down from a fixed $4.30 (−77%) [3].

The dedicated tier moved the other way. A week earlier, on October 1, Nebius raised its on-demand B300 rate from $7.85 to $9.50 (+21%) [3]. On GPUs.io, Verda's on-demand rate is up 27% over 30 days, Lium's 9.4%, and the market median 31.6% over 90 days [4]. Hardware has not moved either: an 8-GPU DGX B300 still anchors at $300,000 to $350,000, unchanged since Q1, and a standalone B300 at about $53,000 [5].
